title: Weak equivalences of Kan complexes give coherent-nerve equivalence edges
statement: Use Kan complexes, weak homotopy equivalences and equivalence edges of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and let $\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}=N_{\mathrm{hc}}(\mathbf{Kan}_{\mathcal W})$ be the subset-poset coherent nerve defined in [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces]. Let $A,B$ be $\mathcal W$-small Kan complexes and let $f:A\to B$ be a simplicial map inducing a bijection on path components and isomorphisms on every based homotopy group after geometric realization. Regard $f$ as the edge from $A$ to $B$ in $\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}$ specified by its vertex in $\operatorname{Fun}(A,B)$. Then there exist a simplicial map $g:B\to A$ and two $2$-simplices of $\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}$ with vertex triples $(A,B,A)$ and $(B,A,B)$ and boundary arrows respectively $(f,g,1_A)$ and $(g,f,1_B)$. In particular this actual edge $f$ is an equivalence edge in the coherent-nerve convention. Empty and disconnected Kan complexes are allowed. The same edge and witnesses remain valid after inclusion in any containing value universe.
